sections.h2: City of San Angelo rate per $100
sections.html:
San Angelo's budget for fiscal year 2026 to 2027 carries a rate of $0.7947 per $100 of valuation. The budget page links to a bill breakdown tool run by the county appraisal district.

The city is only one layer. The other units on your parcel add rates of their own, and the sum is what you owe. Sales tax pieces add to 8.25 percent with the state's 6.25 percent, and the city hotel occupancy rate is 7 percent. The budget office is in City Hall at 72 W. College Ave., and a Taxpayer Impact Statement is available there.

sections.h2: Where to pay or contest San Angelo property tax
sections.html:
San Angelo lies in Tom Green County, and two offices matter: the Tom Green Central Appraisal District at 2302 Pulliam, and the county Tax Assessor-Collector at 113 West Beauregard, whose main office keeps hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Online payment starts with finding your account on the district's website. Choose the Tax Summary tab and click the pay link that appears when a balance is due. E-check and cards both work. The site also offers a tax estimator and explains the protest process.

  • May 15 is the protest deadline for many residential properties. Protests can be sent by email, mail, drop-off or the district's website.
  • Your own deadline appears on the Notice of Appraised Value mailed to you.
  • Drop boxes take payments and documents.

sections.h2: If the review board keeps your value
sections.html: You still have three options: sue in district court, request binding arbitration, or go to the State Office of Administrative Hearings, which handles values above $1,000,000. Whichever you pick, send the undisputed tax by the delinquency date. Keep every notice, and photograph condition problems, since those records carry weight.

sections.h2: Late charges on a San Angelo bill
sections.html:
Expect the bill in October, with payment due January 31 in most cases. Delinquency begins February 1 and brings six percent in penalty along with one percent in interest.

Each month the penalty rises by a point, reaching twelve percent on July 1, and interest continues at one percent monthly. A unit that has hired an attorney may add up to 20 percent. Seniors and disabled homeowners may use four installments, with the first due by February 1.

San Angelo skews older. Roughly 16.8% of residents are 65 or over, so age breaks matter. State law has schools exempt $140,000 of a homestead, and owners 65-plus or disabled get $60,000 more. A city or county can add its own on top.

  • A homestead's appraised value cannot grow more than 10 percent in a year once the exemption has begun.
  • The senior school tax freeze keeps the school bill at the first qualifying year's level.
  • A disabled veteran receives $5,000 off at a rating of 10 to 29 percent, rising to $12,000 at 70 percent or higher, and a 100 percent rating can exempt the homestead completely.

Seniors and disabled owners should apply as soon as they qualify, because the school tax freeze is set from the first qualifying year. The appraisal district posts a guide to the homestead cap, and applications are due to it by April 30. The Comptroller's exemptions page has the statewide list.

sections.h2: San Angelo housing at a glance
sections.html: The city's 100,640 residents are only 0.7 percent above the 2020 base. Of 39,474 households, 61.2 percent own. A typical home is valued near $187,600, rent is $1,153 and median household income is $65,864. Owner costs run $1,536 with a mortgage and $598 without. Roughly 83 percent of people stayed put last year. Medians cover the city as a whole, so an offer in writing or an agent's pricing opinion tells you more about your house.

sections.h2: Steps for a San Angelo protest
sections.html:
A protest is mostly paperwork and timing. Pull your Notice of Appraised Value when it arrives and read the deadline printed on it. The district takes protests by email, mail, drop-off or its website, so choose the method that leaves a record, and keep copies.

  • Check the description of the house against what you know: size, condition, improvements.
  • Take photos of repair problems or other flaws and store them with the notice.
  • Ask for the district's comparable sales and compare them to recent sales near you.
  • Use the district's tax estimator to see what a lower value would mean for the bill.
  • Pay the undisputed tax by the delinquency date while the protest runs.
  • If you cannot attend in person, ask the district how it handles your hearing, and send your evidence early.

A lower value helps you while you own the house, and it gives a buyer a smaller bill to inherit with the sale.

If you inherited a house and are on no recorded deed, you can still request the homestead exemption. Bring the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, the previous owner's death certificate and a recent utility bill, plus court record citations if needed. Ask which papers it wants.

Decide who is allowed to sign the deed before listing. Depending on the estate, that could mean probate, a small estate affidavit or an affidavit of heirship.

Tax owed does not end a sale. Start by asking the Tom Green Central Appraisal District what each unit is owed and whether penalty and interest are open. Pass the statement to the closing agent, who builds the payoff into the settlement sheet so the buyer receives clear title.

The lien dates from January 1, so even a March sale carries that year's tax, and the settlement sheet divides it. Your exemption does not transfer, so a buyer should file their own after closing. With a cash offer, look at the payoff line before you sign and compare the net with what a listing would bring.

sections.h2: What happens to taxes at closing?
sections.html:
Each January 1 a tax claim attaches to the house, so a buyer cannot get clean title while any balance is open. Whoever owned the house that day remains liable for that year after selling.

The closing agent orders the payoff and pays it when funds arrive. Deed recording at the county clerk costs $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page under the state's manual. Before picking a closing date, get each unit's balance from the appraisal district.

If you are behind on San Angelo tax, a written cash offer can build the payoff into the numbers.

faqs.q: What per-$100 rate does San Angelo list?
faqs.a: The budget page shows $0.7947 per $100 of valuation. Other taxing units add theirs, so the full bill is higher.

faqs.q: Can I pay my San Angelo property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. Find your account on the Tom Green Central Appraisal District website, open the Tax Summary tab and use the pay link. E-check and cards are taken.

faqs.q: When must I protest a San Angelo appraisal?
faqs.a: The deadline is May 15, or thirty days after your notice is delivered if that is later. The notice prints your exact date.

faqs.q: How high is sales tax in San Angelo?
faqs.a: The total is 8.25 percent: 1 percent for the city, 0.5 for the San Angelo Development Corporation, 0.5 for Tom Green County and 6.25 for the state.

faqs.q: Can I sell a San Angelo house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid when the sale closes. Get the figure in writing from the Tom Green Central Appraisal District ahead of time.
